A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same RI3D research work and are complete and readable, including all 14 pages, equations, figures, tables, references and four supplementary pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original RI3D evaluations on Mip-NeRF 360 and CO3D, including quantitative results, qualitative comparisons and component ablations (Tables 1–3 and supplementary figures).

after.justification: v2 retains the same original RI3D experiments and ablation results in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain identical depth-based Gaussian initialization, personalized repair and inpainting models, and two-stage optimization procedures and losses.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same sparse novel-view synthesis task on Mip-NeRF 360 scenes and CO3D objects. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain identical comparator sets and attribution of borrowed results. The visual comparisons retain DNGaussian, CoR-GS and FSGS.

E3.justification: The 3-, 6- and 9-view settings, ReconFusion-provided training cameras, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS metrics, preprocessing and optimization budgets are unchanged (Sections 5, 8 and 9).

E4.justification: Both retain the depth-enhancement, single-stage and inpainting-fine-tuning ablations (Table 2 and Figure 8), view-count analysis (Figure 9), and DUSt3R failure example (Figure 10).

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and dataset averages. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and qualitative result images are unchanged. For example, RI3D's 3-view Mip-NeRF 360 results remain 15.74 PSNR, 0.342 SSIM and 0.505 LPIPS; its corresponding CO3D results remain 18.72, 0.628 and 0.385.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(4), and reasoning for the depth-combination objective and optimization losses are identical. No formal assumption, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: separating visible-region reconstruction from missing-region hallucination, using two personalized diffusion models, combining depth estimates for initialization, and optimizing in two stages.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of perceptual quality and CO3D's reduced need for inpainting. The limitations concerning inaccurate DUSt3R depth and inability to handle a single input image are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 8 provides identical GPU requirements, fine-tuning iterations, optimization schedules and view-refresh details. The project URL and third-party inpainting implementation reference are unchanged.

R1.justification: The 49 numbered reference entries and related-work discussion are identical, including the positioning relative to GaussianObject, ReconFusion and CAT3D.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 13 March 2025 to v2 dated 21 January 2026. The manuscript wording, author list, headings and section organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–3 retain the same images, labels, captions, formatting and placement. The main-text and supplementary page layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the same scientific content, experimental evidence, limitations and reproducibility information throughout the paper and supplement. The updated arXiv stamp and PDF metadata produce no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
